I
Syrups
The flavored syrups behind every Signature Matcha, made in-house.
Syrups I · 01
Syrup No. 01
Vanilla Syrup
Ingredients
  • Turbinado Sugar2 cups
  • Water1 cup
  • Vanilla Bean Paste1 tbsp
  • Saltpinch
Yield — ≈ 540 ml
Method
  1. Add the sugar and water to a saucepan over medium heat.
  2. Stir until the sugar dissolves, then bring to a boil.
  3. Take the pot off the heat and stir in the vanilla bean paste and a pinch of salt.
  4. Let cool, then transfer to a bottle or jar.

The pinch of salt isn't a mistake — it rounds out the sweetness and makes the vanilla taste even more like vanilla. Keeps refrigerated for about a month.

Matcha On Ice Cafe Page 3
Syrups I · 02
Syrup No. 02
Banana Bread Syrup
Ingredients
  • Unsalted Butter1 tbsp
  • Bananas, mashed2
  • Brown Sugar1 cup
  • Water1 cup
  • Ground Cinnamon1 tsp
  • Vanilla Bean Paste1 tsp
  • Saltpinch
Method
  1. Add the butter to a saucepan over medium heat. Add the mashed bananas and brown sugar.
  2. Let caramelize for 2–3 minutes, then add the water, cinnamon and salt. Mix and bring to a boil.
  3. Reduce heat and simmer for 7–10 minutes.
  4. Turn off the heat and stir in the vanilla.
  5. Let cool to room temperature, then blend or strain.

Store in an airtight jar and refrigerate for up to 3 weeks.

Matcha On Ice Cafe Page 4
Syrups I · 03
Syrup No. 03
Strawberry Syrup
Ingredients
  • Strawberries, fresh or frozen275 g
  • Sugar325 g
  • Water325 ml
Yield — ≈ 850 ml
Method
  1. Add the strawberries, sugar and hot water to a pot.
  2. Turn the heat to medium-high and stir to help dissolve the sugar.
  3. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 8 minutes.
  4. Remove from heat and blend with an immersion blender until smooth.
  5. Let cool, then transfer to a jar or bottle.

Keeps refrigerated for 3–4 weeks.

Matcha On Ice Cafe Page 5
Syrups I · 04
Syrup No. 04
Mango Syrup
Ingredients
  • Mango, fresh or frozen250 g
  • Sugar1 cup (≈ 180 g)
  • Water1 cup (≈ 220 ml)
Yield — ≈ 600 ml (20 fl oz)
Method
  1. Peel and chop the mango, then blend until smooth to make a purée — a small splash of water helps it along, if needed.
  2. Pour the purée into a saucepan, add the sugar and water, and stir to combine.
  3. Bring to a gentle boil over medium heat, whisking continuously until the sugar fully dissolves.
  4. Remove from heat and let cool completely.
  5. Transfer to a clean bottle or airtight container.

Store refrigerated for up to 2 weeks — shake well before each use.

II
Cold Foam
The base cold foam used across the Signature Matchas.
Cold Foam II · About
Cold Foam
About Cold Foam

Cold foam comes together from three components: two parts Heavy Cream, which brings fat, creaminess and structure; one part Whole Milk, which lightens the texture; and one part Syrup or purée, which brings flavor, sugar and liquid.

It's built in two stages. First, air is whipped into the mixture, so it gains volume and grows in size. Then that air is textured into the base, giving the foam its velvety, light finish.

Base Ratio
2 : 1 : 1 (Cream : Milk : Syrup)

For every 4 oz of base — 2 oz heavy cream, 1 oz whole milk, 1 oz syrup or purée.

Matcha On Ice Cafe Page 8
Cold Foam II · Recipe
Cold Foam
Recipe
Batch — Makes ≈ 32 oz
  • Heavy Cream16 oz
  • Whole Milk8 oz
  • Syrup8 oz
Method
  1. Combine the heavy cream, whole milk and syrup in a 2:1:1 ratio.
  2. Whip to incorporate air — the mixture will grow in volume.
  3. Continue whipping to texture that air into the base, until velvety and light.
  4. Batch ahead of the shift and keep refrigerated for quick service.
